title: Post-pair synthesis: inference candidate — Ishaan Mehta
body:
Context and quick summary:
- Pair session on 2025-01-14 (60m) focused on optimizing a KV-cache eviction policy for a toy transformer serving stack. Candidate: ‘Leah Carter’ (senior inference engineer candidate).
- Goal of session: evaluate systems intuition, tradeoff thinking, low-latency heuristics, and collaboration style under time pressure.

Immediate impressions (first 10m):
- Calm, methodical; asked clarifying Qs (latency SLOs, workload distribution, request size P95) instead of jumping to code.
- Sketches architecture quickly: in-memory KV + write-ahead log + background compactor. Good initial mental model.

What they did well:
- Tradeoffs: Enumerated three eviction strategies (LRU, frequency-aware TTL, recent-prefix-pin) and mapped each to workload types (short-context chat vs. long-context doc summarization).
- Cost/latency framing: explicitly called out GPU memory pressure vs. host memory vs. network cost, and proposed pinning hot prefixes to GPU for critical clients.
- Incremental proof: implemented a minimal simulation (python-esque pseudocode) to show hit-rate delta for LRU vs. freq-aware on a zipf-like access distribution.
- Safety nets: suggested graceful degradation — fall back to prefix truncation rather than full eviction under memory thrash.

Where they struggled or had gaps:
- Complexity accounting: initial simulation didn’t model KV lookup latency variance (hash table vs. sharded LRU) — when prompted, candidate acknowledged but didn’t iterate to fix within time.
- Concurrency: proposed a lock-striping sketch but didn’t discuss false-sharing or memory barriers; their assumption of cheap mutexes on hot paths needs validation.
- Quantitative baseline: no rough numbers for expected token-level latency impact of GPU pinned cache vs. host DRAM; relied on qualitative statements.

Behavioral / collaboration notes:
- Communicative: narrated thinking aloud, responded well to hints; accepted small pivots when interviewer suggested multi-tenant noise.
- Ownership instincts: asked about customer tiers and suggested different policies per tier (enterprise clients get pinned prefixes).
- Code hygiene: variable names/pseudocode were clear; asked to factor out simulation harness as a function.

Specific examples from session (paraphrased):
- "If 80% of requests are short chat turns, an LRU with prefix pinning for the top 5% of prefixes gives ~2–3x hit-rate improvement for tail latency-sensitive requests."
- Proposed metric: client-level cache-hit heatmap + per-prefix P99 token latency to trigger auto-pin.

Red flags (things to validate in follow-up):
- Threading assumptions: relies on coarse-grained locks; ask for scalable concurrency plan for 64+ cores and multi-GPU nodes.
- Production experience surface: has strong simulation and toy implementations but fewer examples of deploying rolling upgrades for stateful caches at scale (need concrete postmortem or runbook examples).

Recommended follow-ups (concrete interview ask):
1) Design interview: ask them to design a multi-tenant KV cache that supports eviction policies, shard rebalancing, and live migration between nodes. Goal: probe rebalancing, state transfer, and backpressure.
2) Systems deep dive: give a concurrent LRU implementation with heavy contention and ask to refactor to lock-free or per-shard approach; measure and interpret perf counters.
3) Past-project concrete: request one pager describing a production incident they owned (timeline, mitigation, root cause, postmortem).

Hire recommendation (tentative):
- Strengths: strong systems thinking, good product-oriented tradeoff reasoning, collaborative in pairing.
- Gaps: needs clearer evidence of running stateful infra at 10s–100s of nodes, and more rigorous concurrency/latency quantification.
- Recommendation: advance to a focused follow-up loop (design + incident writeup). Consider leveling at Senior IC with interview checks for scalability experience before offering Staff.

Suggested ramp plan if hired (6–12 weeks):
- Week 0–2: onboarding + read-only access to our KV/cache telemetry dashboards; small bugfix to the compactor.
- Week 3–6: own a single-customer cache policy rollout (canary + telemetry gating).
- Week 7–12: lead rebalancing prototype and run a perf experiment comparing per-prefix pinning vs. global LRU on representative workloads.

Unresolved questions to capture in hiring doc:
- Which customers (internal/external) currently rely on prefix pinning? Any existing SLO breaches tied to cache thrash?
- Can we share a simple perf artifact (microbench) ahead of follow-up to calibrate their expectations on lock costs and host vs. device lookup latencies?

Quick action items (for panel coordinator):
- Share this note with Rina and Avery; request scheduling of design + postmortem follow-up.
- Assign an interviewer with SRE/Runtime background for the concurrency deep dive.
- Ask candidate for 1–2 pages describing a production incident.

Personal reflection (private):
- I feel comfortable with candidate’s instincts; the missing production-scale evidence is common and addressable with the right follow-ups. They have the product sensitivity we value at Redwood (explicitly mapping tradeoffs to customer tiers).
- Candidate likely strong addition to team if they can demonstrate operational ownership in follow-up.

End of note.
